approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from accepted high-scoring molecules selected by score band. It either joins connected fragments from two parents, sometimes followed by mutation, or makes an ordinary mutation walk. Each mutation call retries the same seven primitive edit families with fixed weights until a valid product is found or its bound is reached. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable identity and duplicate checks form fresh surplus pools. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated posterior draws choose the evaluated offspring. Accepted raw scores update the archive and greedy survivor population.
approach.novelty: Add magnitude-sensitive feedback to the existing mutation-operator lottery. Only an evaluated, accepted ordinary product with exactly one mutation call supplies credit to its uniquely successful primitive. Its nonnegative improvement over its actual generating source is scaled by the accepted archive available before emission and converted to a bounded reward. Smoothed accumulated rewards reweight the unchanged operator repertoire once per suggestion. Earlier operator-success weighting increased local win frequency while reducing gain size and final scores; this variant tests a different credit statistic under selective evaluation. It retains all composite generation and continuation, unlike removing those routes to simplify attribution. The current siblings test other proposal, representation, identity or selector boundaries, not this accepted single-call magnitude-credit law.

observed_bottleneck: The complete current-profile code Parent n-62daf219c70a has mean final Top-1 0.5956696497334577 and seed-macro population SD 0.02659287062806747. Its mutation operator weights remain fixed at [0.28,0.20,0.16,0.12,0.10,0.08,0.06] even after accepted outcomes reveal heterogeneous source gains. A read-only reconstruction of all fifteen published Parent task logs, joined to their accepted trajectories and complete pre-emission archives, finds 2536 eligible ordinary single-call accepted products among 4350 emissions, with 403 strict source wins and 466 eligible products requiring internal retries. The remaining 1814 accepted outputs are excluded from this auxiliary credit, including 1492 crossovers and composite/continuation histories; exclusion reason counts overlap. Ninety-three eligible products are terminal and cannot expose later allocation. Retrospective magnitude arithmetic would change normalized weights at all 420 post-initial Parent boundaries, but the Parent never ran that rule; these are opportunity counts, not Child activation or efficacy. Two close-ring cases have a primitive checker string different from the final stable emitted string, while the returned checked graph serializes to that emitted identity. The exact emitted/accepted join must preserve the inherited normalization chain rather than add a primitive-string equality gate. The direct statistic counterexample n-9ab62999124d is an L16 fixed-source neighborhood walk with one generating operator per accepted neighbor. Its binary accepted-success weighting changed 2250 operator draws and produced 1594 accepted changed-choice neighbors, yet source wins rose only from 462 to 471 while mean positive gain fell from 0.024939 to 0.021552, archive gains fell from 238 to 230, and its paired macro endpoint changed by -0.022183724645278995. Generation yield also fell from 0.823084 to 0.785624. This identifies magnitude versus event frequency as an unresolved question, not a proven cause or fix. The different L01 parent-credit test n-030a6ccbba7c likewise increased incumbent-gain counts from 218 to 228 while mean positive increment fell from 0.023111 to 0.020678 and its own paired endpoint fell by 0.02157946287432137. Those historical Parents and profiles are not substitutes for the current comparison. Current controls n-dbee08307e86 and n-01b48dd09404 lose 0.02686763734135833 and 0.12438789088524467 when ordinary continuation or composite predictive allocation is removed. They motivate retaining both useful components and treating observed operator rewards as selected associations, not independent operator efficacy.
hypothesis: At each real suggestion boundary, reweight the unchanged mutation-operator mixture by smoothed bounded gain-magnitude credit from exactly joined earlier accepted ordinary single-call offspring, freezing positive weights throughout that suggestion and preserving every inherited generation route.

finding_summary.headline: Magnitude credit raises simple-source gains, but incumbent progress and endpoint mean fall
finding_summary.insights:
Magnitude-sensitive allocation improved the selected simple-source gain measurements without preserving stronger search progress. This narrows the motivating frequency-versus-size question: the eligible gain-size prediction succeeded, but it did not protect absolute candidate quality, incumbent advances or endpoints. Sources and archive scales were also lower, and the GP selected which outcomes could teach the weights. The result therefore supports a negative contribution from this particular added allocation rule under the tested composition; it does not establish that magnitude credit is worse than binary credit or that any primitive is causally ineffective.

The learned rule also affected failed inner trials, ordinary continuation and crossover finishing, none of which supplies its own credit. A successful one-call output after inner retries can still train its uniquely successful operator. Historical reward enrichment in those choices is an allocation result, not evidence that credit transfers as future efficacy. Rare operators retain optimistic smoothing, and invalid attempts remain invisible to the accepted-only reward. The preserved continuation and crossover channels, as well as terminal survivors, continue to produce useful outcomes outside consumed credit.

The chemical assessment still finds useful compact amines, lactams and aromatic alternatives alongside large repeated assemblies, unusual peripheral bonds, difficult rings and unspecified stereochemistry. A positive source gain or retained descendant can preserve those liabilities. Neither the credit labels nor lineage counts isolate a chemical explanation for the endpoint loss. The experiment supplies an exposed complete score failure under the registered review condition; changing provenance, suppressing composite routes or retuning the reward would be a new intervention.
finding_summary.results:
The credit and allocation mechanism executed as registered. Of 2,567 eligible accepted one-call outputs, 2,473 were consumed at a later real suggestion; 94 terminal outputs remained unused for allocation. Failed internal retries did not become extra credit trials, and composite outcomes remained uncredited raw observations. All 435 frozen weight calculations and 83,314 recorded primitive choices passed independent checks. The first fifteen suggestions matched the Parent, while all 420 later laws changed. Fixed-weight replay on the same recorded random states changed 36,657 primitive choices. These reached 1,700 accepted descendants; 917 later served as parents and 400 remained in final populations.

Within the eligible cohort, source wins rose from 403 to 452 and mean positive gain rose from 0.023041 to 0.025333. Positive gain per eligible observation also rose, from 0.003661 to 0.004461. Yet mean absolute offspring score fell from 0.404728 to 0.374110, and eligible incumbent advances fell from 164 to 147. Across the whole search, wins rose from 629 to 708 while mean positive-win size slipped from 0.024527 to 0.024071 and incumbent advances fell from 258 to 243.

All fifteen task runs completed. Mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.566674, a paired change of -0.028996 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were -0.086822, +0.053583 and -0.053749; nine of fifteen task-seed endpoints declined and six improved. Seed population SD rose from 0.026593 to 0.033955. Every pool and announced batch completed, although primitive validity decreased and one call exhausted its twelve internal attempts.

molecular.headline: Aryl amines and medium-ring lactams coexist with reactive halogen bonds, cyanates and uncertain ring geometry
molecular.overall_character: Child n-9d0376974738 and code Parent n-62daf219c70a have complete paired Search Seed 0, 1 and 2 panels under the supplied frozen profile: child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with no profile mismatches. All thirty supplied trajectories and corresponding Search logs were present and read. Each node has 4,500 evaluated records, including 4,350 optimizer proposals; each task has 900 records and 870 optimizer proposals. No task or comparison trajectory is missing. The supplied means are 0.566673708256114 for Child and 0.5956696497334577 for Parent, with seed changes -0.08682173267617399, +0.05358292956691191 and -0.05374902132276893. These are protocol results, not an activation or mediation finding. The output includes styryl aza-aromatics, N-halogen indole carboxamides, linked aza-heterocycles with cyanates, large hydrazone/urea-like assemblies, flexible and cyclic aryl amines, medium-ring lactams and bridged carbonyl systems, and fluorinated imino/dicarbonyl heterocycles. Median optimizer heavy-atom counts in fixed task order are 25, 39, 33, 31 and 27, versus Parent 25, 33, 31, 30 and 27. The second task includes a 76-heavy-atom seed leader and reaches 119 heavy atoms in its evaluated sample. Child ring-closure-string incidence ranges from 0.9575 to 0.9862 and aromatic-string incidence from 0.9506 to 0.9782. These are molecule-level text-feature incidences, not fractions of aromatic atoms or perceived ring counts. Rings and aromaticity are rich. Diversity is moderate across seeds and tasks, with much narrower leading families within a seed. Recognizable amines, lactams and aza-aromatic frameworks coexist with N-halogen, O-halogen, N-O and N-S bonds, cyanates, constrained unsaturation and difficult bridges. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable and drug-likeness weak overall, without implying that every molecule is implausible. All tasks have zero stereocentre-string incidence despite potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged centres. The charge-string exception is a low-scoring small nitrile oxide in median_2; this is not systematic protonation-state coverage. Neutral amine strings still contain basic centres. Size and ring descriptions use read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 readings of the trusted structures, stored in .slots/r0018-01-improve-L01/molecular/trajectory_chemistry_audit.json. Neither canonical validity, ring perception nor supplied scores establish synthesis, stability, geometry or biological activity. The full trajectories distinguish late proposals from each seed's retained best molecule. The output/credit distinction is audited in .slots/r0018-01-improve-L01/molecular/credit_exposure_audit.json and summarized in credit_summary.json. Child has 2,567 accepted ordinary single-call outputs eligible by actual provenance, including 610 that required internal retries. Of these, 2,473 are consumed for credit at a later real suggestion and 94 belong to the terminal batch and remain unconsumed. The last 150 emissions have no subsequent credit-consumption boundary; among their eligible outputs, 69 remain in final populations. A retained terminal molecule does not demonstrate later allocation use. The other evaluated routes include 345 ordinary continuation products, 963 pure crossovers and 475 crossover-finishing products; they remain evaluated and potentially retained, but do not supply this auxiliary credit. No evaluated case with a later failed call after exactly one successful primitive was observed; the registered exclusion of such a case remains outside that evaluated exposure. Actual recorded-choice replay checked 83,314 primitive selections. Nonbaseline frozen weights were used in 80,466 choices: 53,920 ordinary first-call choices, 11,201 continuation choices and 15,345 crossover-finishing choices; 20,561 of these were internal retries, an overlapping category. This records where the law was used, not where a chemical benefit was caused. Eight credited outputs have an early primitive checker spelling different from the stable emitted key; the returned-graph/final-admission/accepted chain is preserved. This is normalization provenance, not another chemical edit or a synthetic-quality guarantee. The complete Parent supplies 2,536 retrospectively eligible outputs, including 466 with retries, but used fixed weights and never consumed this credit. Unselected pool alternatives have no new labels and no credit trials. All retained claims use recorded observations and a replay of the unchanged score/serial survivor ordering, checked against every batch receipt. Later reuse and ancestry do not identify endpoint contribution. Historical counterexamples retain their scope: binary operator-success credit in the different L16 fixed-source walk n-9ab62999124d increased source-win frequency while its paired endpoint fell by 0.022183724645278995; the distinct parent-allocation test n-030a6ccbba7c also had more, smaller gains and a paired decrease of 0.02157946287432137. Those Parents, profiles and selection conditions are not substitutes for this comparison. The present fixed-weight contrast does not isolate magnitude versus binary credit. Shared-Parent sibling results are nonindependent, and no combined effect, sibling source inheritance or resolution of the separate partial L07 continuation mapping is claimed.

per_task.generated_character: The three seed leaders have 24, 25 and 24 heavy atoms, each with three rings. Seed 0 forms a dimethoxy/chloromethyl-substituted aza-aromatic fused ring joined through an alkene to pyridine; it lacks an amide and an N-halogen bond. Seeds 1 and 2 instead retain indole-anilide carboxamides: the first carries N-F or N-Cl on the amide, chloromethyl ether and an N-amino indole; the second has N-F amide and N-S substitution. Median size remains the Parent's 25 heavy atoms, but its seed-0 cumulene and seed-2 vicinal-diketone leaders are replaced by different compact families. The three Child leaders are ordinary single-call products whose accepted gains were later consumed; that provenance does not establish the chemical merit of their inherited cores.
liabilities: N-F and N-Cl amides are different environments from ordinary aryl C-F/C-Cl bonds; N-amino and N-sulfenyl substitution require their own reactivity assessment.
The seed-0 leader has a chloromethyl group and unspecified alkene geometry despite its more conventional aza-aromatic organization.
A credited scalar gain can preserve a reactive scaffold; the credit does not demonstrate stability or synthetic accessibility.
missing_features: Conventional peripheral bond environments are not consistently retained in the amide families: high-scoring examples still use N-halogen and N-S/N-N attachments and chloromethyl ether groups. The aza-aromatic alkene is a counterexample to a universal need for those liabilities.
Chemically independent plausible alternatives remain limited within each seed, despite clearly different families across seeds.
The alkene/imine geometries and any potentially stereogenic saturated products are unspecified; no exact missing target pharmacophore follows from these scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Child seed leaders score 0.43299980873877003, 0.46092619585962435 and 0.4394278959350887, versus Parent 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.438972502037081. The seed-1 N-F and N-Cl amide variants tie at 0.46092619585962435, but the strong seed-0 aza-aromatic alkene shows that neither an amide nor an N-halogen bond is universally required. Replacing the latter's alkene linker with an imine gives 0.4067656765249372, and replacing one methoxy group with ethyl gives 0.3131060688534292. These local comparisons associate reward with the compact aromatic/polar arrangement and substituent placement. A much larger linked indole-amide proposal scores 6.51345698395413e-11, and the small cyclic peroxide C1COO1 scores 0.0. Familiar fragments, ring presence or added complexity alone do not reproduce the leading organization.

per_task.generated_character: Median optimizer size rises from Parent 33 to Child 39 heavy atoms. Seed 0 leads with a 44-heavy-atom densely linked aza-heterocycle/dione assembly, bromomethyl/thioether substituents and a three-membered nitrogen-containing ring motif. Seed 1 reaches a 35-heavy-atom aza-aromatic system bearing two O-linked cyanates, an O-formyl group, carbon-bound fluorines and an O/S-containing ring. Seed 2 forms a 76-heavy-atom flexible repeated assembly rich in hydrazone, N-N, carbonyl and urea-like links; its proposal median is 56 heavy atoms. The Parent's strongest seed instead reaches a compact 30-heavy-atom linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione framework. The Child seed-0 leader is pure crossover, the seed-2 leader is ordinary continuation and the seed-1 leader is an eligible terminal close-ring product whose feedback is never consumed for another suggestion. These are distinct output paths, not one credited-operator cohort.
liabilities: O-C#N cyanates, O-O-C#N links in relatives, and bromomethyl/thioether attachments remain chemically specific concerns.
The seed-0 leader combines a three-membered heteroatom-containing ring motif with extensive unsaturated ring connectivity; representability alone cannot establish feasible geometry.
The seed-2 repeated N-N/imine/urea-like assembly has substantial size and flexibility; many carbonyl groups do not by themselves establish drug-like behavior.
missing_features: Consistent control of repeated assembly and context-preserving simplification is missing in the evaluated record; useful compact aza-heterocycles coexist with large carbonyl/N-N-rich structures.
Stable local alternatives to cyanate, peroxide and halomethyl functionality are not established at every leading arrangement. Carbon-bound nitriles and O-linked cyanates should not be conflated.
The crowded small-ring/bridged systems and flexible hydrazone-rich structures lack demonstrated geometry, stereochemical or tautomeric identity. Their scores do not establish an accessible synthesis.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dione scores 0.548381482770623; a small peroxide-linked quinoline fragment scores 0.5100965759438103 and isolated chlorine 0.5. Child seed leaders reach 0.6228723679445394, 0.6271676300578035 and 0.6066514450519738, versus Parent 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013. The larger and more nitrogen-rich assemblies therefore do not recreate the Parent's favorable seed-0 organization. The seed-1 leader's less fused analogue scores 0.6247251236943375; an additional O-O cyanate-containing late relative scores 0.616421568627451. These nearby scores do not require every ring closure or reactive attachment. A simpler four-ring seed-0 aza-heterocyclic relative scores 0.6178901312591152, near the more crowded leader, while a 77-heavy-atom final seed-2 repeat assembly ties its 76-heavy-atom leader at 0.6066514450519738. More atoms and repeated functional groups are not uniformly rewarded.

per_task.generated_character: The three leaders have 28, 30 and 33 heavy atoms. Seed 0 produces a flexible enamine/secondary-amine chain linking a trichlorophenyl thioether to a methoxyphenyl group. Seed 1 has a cyclic diamine joined to aryl groups through a cyclobutene-containing framework, with an aryl O-S linkage. Seed 2 retains an N-propyl pyrrolidine attached to a brominated, fluorinated bridged O/N ring system and a phenolic biaryl region. Median size is 33 heavy atoms versus Parent 31. All seeds retain available amines and aromatic surfaces, unlike a claim that the generator lacks basic centres. The Parent favors flexible tertiary amines and pyrrolidine/thioether or aminoalkyl cyclic frameworks near the score ceiling. The Child leaders arise from credited single-call append, close-ring and delete-atom outputs respectively; those operator names do not isolate the value of the complete molecules.
liabilities: The leading flexible molecule contains an enamine, substantial aryl chlorine and thioether chemistry; stability and solubility are unmeasured.

Other high-scoring products carry an O-S linkage, N-O groups, halogenated crowded bridges or small unsaturated rings; lower N-halogen incidence than the Parent does not establish broad chemical-quality control.
Potential stereogenic centres remain unspecified in the familiar pyrrolidine and cyclic-diamine families as well as the more difficult bridges.
missing_features: Stereochemically defined versions of the successful saturated rings, benzylic centres and bridged O/N systems are absent from the evaluated strings.
Conventional local alternatives and credible ring geometry are not consistently retained, even though simpler high-scoring cyclic-amine structures are present.
Explicit protonation-state coverage is not established; neutral notation should not be mistaken for lack of basic amines, and adding more amines is not the demonstrated missing capability.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders have 29, 29 and 28 heavy atoms. Seed 1 leads with an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen/dicarbonyl ring, an N-fluorinated amino five-membered heteroaromatic ring, and a saturated cyclopentyl group bearing three carbon-bound fluorines and chlorine. transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and is reproduced in n-62daf219c70a; it recurs in n-9d0376974738 on complete matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per objective under the frozen profile. Evaluated or retained leaders carry N-halogen, N-S, N-O, O-S, cyanate and halomethyl chemistry. Credited positive-gain outputs can retain those groups. Strong aza-aromatic alkenes without N-halogen/amide groups and simpler high-scoring pyrrolidine/O,N-ring examples are counterexamples to a universal need for them.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional bond environments while retaining favorable scaffold relationships.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer bond-environment-aware alternatives that preserve useful local scaffold and functional-group relationships learned from feedback. Distinguish ordinary carbon-bound halogens and familiar amine, amide or thioether environments from unusual attachments. Operator credit, canonical validity and positive gain do not establish synthetic accessibility or a universal filtering benefit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a and remains in the current n-9d0376974738 matched three-seed panel. Structures include a three-membered heteroatom-containing ring motif, crowded brominated O/N bridges, small fused oxygen/carbocyclic rings, medium-ring polyamine lactams and large aromatic-labelled nitrogen rings. The strongest fluorinated leader lacks a cyclic cumulene, and simpler conventional-looking cyclic-amine alternatives score highly, so the most difficult motifs are not universal requirements.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish a representable ring graph from credible unsaturation, aromaticity or bridge geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide alternative ring topologies sensitive to ring size, bond geometry, heteroatom arrangement and bridge connectivity while preserving useful chemical context. Do not equate ring counts, aromatic labels, a close-ring gain or a canonical string with feasible geometry. These observations do not support banning every small, fused or medium ring or assigning one edit a causal endpoint value.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Previously observed in n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a; all five n-9d0376974738 tasks again have zero stereocentre-string incidence under the matched three-seed observation budget. Cited molecules include multiply fluorinated cyclopentyl centres, substituted pyrrolidines, bridged O/N systems and unspecified alkene/imine arrangements. The lone charge-marked small nitrile oxide does not provide systematic protonation coverage, while basic amines already occur in neutral notation.
transferable_gaps.gap: Emitted molecules lack specified stereochemical identity where saturated, bridged or geometrically isomeric features require it.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or resolve stereochemical identity when warranted, distinguishing achiral and configurationally unstable cases. Treat protonation and tautomerism separately. Accepted identity joins and normalization provenance preserve the strings supplied; they cannot restore missing stereochemical content or demonstrate a stereochemical score penalty.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Context-retention limitations were present in n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a and recur in n-9d0376974738 under complete matched Search conditions. Small hydrocarbon, halogen, peroxide and nitrile-oxide outputs reach observed floors. One seed instead produces a 76-heavy-atom hydrazone/urea-like leader and repeated larger relatives without recreating the Parent's favorable compact family. Compact aryl amines and aza-aromatics remain high-scoring, and simpler local alternatives can approach more crowded leaders.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve useful molecular context while controlling fragmentation and repeated assembly.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Keep coherent functional-group context when simplifying or recombining structures, and distinguish useful elaboration from repetition. These conditional observations justify neither a fixed minimum size nor automatic preference for larger molecules. The presence of credited delete/append edits and uncredited continuation or crossover products does not identify which route caused the size distribution.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-9d0376974738 compared with complete n-62daf219c70a Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per objective. A credited single-call fluorine append improves its source while retaining N-F bonds and an unusual nitrogen ring; other leaders remain local amide, aryl-amine or lactam variants. Different seeds do reach different families, so this is not global structural collapse. Terminal eligible leaders, continuation products and crossover leaders demonstrate useful chemistry outside consumed credit. Historical n-9ab62999124d and n-030a6ccbba7c remain failed more-but-smaller-gain counterexamples under different mechanisms and conditions.
transferable_gaps.gap: Local source improvements can preserve a narrow chemically questionable family without supplying independent plausible alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Assess coverage through complete molecular arrangements and feasible alternatives, rather than gain events or operator names alone. Preserve the distinction between credit-eligible observations, actual weighted exposure, unlabelled pool options and later retained chemistry. The current fixed-weight comparison cannot isolate magnitude from binary credit; shared-Parent siblings and descendant ancestry do not identify additive or causal chemical effects.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
